questions.text: Sweet potato and carrot store food in their

questions.text: Onion is an example of a
questions.explanation: An onion bulb has fleshy leaf bases that store food around a short stem.

questions.text: Ginger stores food in a
questions.explanation: Ginger is a horizontal underground stem called a rhizome.

questions.text: Which structure carries manufactured food from the leaves to other parts?
questions.explanation: Phloem transports sugars made in photosynthesis.

questions.text: The waxy layer covering a leaf surface is the
questions.explanation: The cuticle reduces water loss from the leaf surface.

questions.text: The stalk that attaches a leaf to the stem is the
questions.explanation: The petiole (leaf stalk) holds the lamina out to the light.

questions.text: The part of a stem between two nodes is the
questions.explanation: Nodes are where leaves join; the length between them is the internode.

questions.text: A bud found in the angle between a leaf and the stem is
questions.explanation: Axillary buds grow in the leaf axil and can form side branches.

questions.text: Prop roots that grow from the stem and support plants such as maize are
questions.explanation: Adventitious roots arise from parts other than the radicle, such as the stem.

questions.text: Which tissue in a dicotyledonous stem divides to increase its girth?
questions.explanation: The cambium produces new xylem and phloem, making the stem thicker.

questions.text: Tendrils in plants such as pumpkin help the plant to
questions.explanation: Tendrils coil round supports so the weak stem can climb towards light.

questions.text: Which of these is a monocotyledonous plant?
questions.explanation: Maize has one seed leaf, parallel veins and fibrous roots.

questions.text: The spines of cactus are modified
questions.explanation: Spines are reduced leaves that cut down water loss in dry places.

questions.text: Mistletoe obtains water and minerals from its host using
questions.explanation: Haustoria are special roots that grow into the host's tissues.

questions.text: In a cross-section of a dicot root, xylem is usually arranged
options: in a ring of bundles near the edge
in a star shape at the centre
questions.explanation: Dicot roots have a central star-shaped xylem with phloem between its arms.

questions.text: In a monocot stem, the vascular bundles are
questions.explanation: Scattered vascular bundles are a feature of monocot stems such as maize.

questions.text: The main function of the leaf is
questions.explanation: Leaves are adapted to trap light and make food.

questions.text: The cassava root is useful to the plant because it
questions.explanation: Cassava roots are swollen with stored starch.

questions.text: Which part of the plant anchors it firmly in the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots hold the plant in place and absorb water.

questions.text: Cocoyam stores food in a
questions.explanation: A cocoyam corm is a short, swollen, upright underground stem.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a herbaceous plant?
options: a plant with a soft, green, non-woody stem
a tall tree with a woody trunk
questions.explanation: Herbaceous plants have soft stems and little or no wood.

questions.text: Which organisms are the main decomposers in nutrient cycles?
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.text: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria such as Rhizobium are found in

questions.text: Plants absorb nitrogen from the soil mainly in the form of

questions.text: The process in which nitrites are changed into nitrates is

questions.text: The breakdown of proteins in dead organisms to release ammonia is called
questions.explanation: Decomposers release ammonia from dead proteins; this is ammonification (putrefaction).

questions.text: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Green plants take in carbon dioxide to make food.

questions.text: Burning firewood adds which gas to the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Combustion of carbon-containing fuels releases carbon dioxide.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT add carbon dioxide to the air?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide; the others release it.

questions.text: Waterlogged soils lose nitrogen mainly through
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria thrive in waterlogged, airless soil and release nitrogen gas.

questions.text: The loss of water vapour from plants into the air is part of the water cycle and is called
questions.explanation: Transpiration returns water from leaves to the atmosphere.

questions.text: Rain, snow and hail falling to the ground are forms of
questions.explanation: Precipitation brings water from clouds back to the land and sea.

questions.text: Fossil fuels are part of the carbon cycle because they
options: are carbon from organisms that lived long ago
questions.explanation: Coal and crude oil formed from dead organisms, so burning them releases stored carbon.

questions.text: Which organism takes in carbon dioxide during the day?
questions.explanation: Only green plants photosynthesise, taking in carbon dioxide in light.

questions.text: The oxygen cycle is closely linked to the carbon cycle because
options: photosynthesis releases oxygen and respiration uses it
oxygen is made by burning fuels
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis and respiration exchange carbon dioxide and oxygen in opposite directions.

questions.text: Planting legumes such as cowpea improves soil fertility because they
options: add nitrogen compounds to the soil
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules enrich the soil with nitrogen.

questions.text: Animals obtain nitrogen mainly by
questions.explanation: Animals get nitrogen as protein in their food.

questions.text: Nitrosomonas converts
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas carries out the first step of nitrification.

questions.text: Large-scale burning of fossil fuels is linked to
questions.explanation: Extra carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, causing global warming.

questions.text: In the water cycle, water seeping into the ground is called
questions.explanation: Infiltration refills soil water and groundwater.

questions.text: Which of the following is the main reservoir of nitrogen?
questions.explanation: About 78% of air is nitrogen gas.

questions.text: Decay is faster in warm, moist conditions because
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi grow and work fastest when warm and moist.

questions.text: Which two processes in the carbon cycle are exact opposites in what they take in and give out?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis takes in CO₂ and gives out O₂; respiration does the reverse.

questions.text: Cutting down forests affects the carbon cycle by
options: reducing the removal of carbon dioxide from the air
questions.explanation: Fewer trees means less carbon dioxide taken up by photosynthesis.

questions.text: The correct order of classification groups from largest to smallest is
options: species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
kingdom, class, phylum, order, genus, family, species
phylum, kingdom, class, order, family, species, genus
kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the largest group and species the smallest.

questions.text: In the scientific name Homo sapiens, sapiens is the
questions.explanation: The first word is the genus and the second is the species.

questions.text: Who introduced the binomial system of naming organisms?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus gave each organism a genus and a species name.

questions.text: Bacteria belong to the kingdom
questions.explanation: Monera (prokaryotes) have no true nucleus.

questions.text: Amoeba and Paramecium belong to the kingdom
questions.explanation: They are single-celled organisms with a true nucleus.

questions.text: Which feature is shared by all vertebrates?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates have a vertebral column.

questions.text: Animals with feathers and beaks belong to the class

questions.text: The toad belongs to the class
questions.explanation: Amphibians have moist skin and live part of their life in water.

questions.text: Which group of animals has an exoskeleton and jointed legs?
questions.explanation: Arthropods such as insects and crabs have jointed limbs and a hard outer skeleton.

questions.text: Earthworms belong to the phylum
questions.explanation: Annelids have soft, ringed (segmented) bodies.

questions.text: Snails belong to the phylum
questions.explanation: Molluscs have soft bodies, often protected by a shell.

questions.text: How many legs does an adult insect have?
questions.explanation: Insects have three pairs of jointed legs.

questions.text: Spiders differ from insects because spiders have
questions.explanation: Spiders (arachnids) have four pairs of legs and two body parts.

questions.text: Plants that produce seeds in cones, such as pine, are called
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms have naked seeds, usually in cones.

questions.text: Flowering plants are called
questions.explanation: Angiosperms produce seeds enclosed in fruits.

questions.text: Mosses belong to the group
questions.explanation: Bryophytes are small, non-vascular plants such as mosses and liverworts.

questions.text: Ferns differ from mosses because ferns have
questions.explanation: Ferns (pteridophytes) have xylem and phloem; mosses do not.

questions.text: Which of these is a cold-blooded animal?
questions.explanation: Reptiles cannot keep a constant body temperature; their temperature changes with the surroundings.

questions.text: Which characteristic is used to place an animal in the class Mammalia?
options: it has mammary glands and hair
questions.explanation: Mammals feed their young on milk and have hair or fur.

questions.text: Fish breathe with
questions.explanation: Gills take oxygen from water.

questions.text: A virus is not placed in any of the five kingdoms mainly because it
options: is not made of cells and reproduces only inside living cells
questions.explanation: Viruses are not cellular and show life only inside a host cell.

questions.text: Which of these organisms makes its own food?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra has chloroplasts; Rhizopus and Mucor are fungi and Amoeba is a protist.

questions.text: Which of these is a characteristic of fungi?
options: they feed on dead or living matter and have no chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Fungi are saprophytes or parasites and lack chlorophyll.

questions.text: The snake belongs to the class
questions.explanation: Snakes are reptiles: dry, scaly skin and they lay leathery eggs.

questions.text: Which structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is partially permeable and regulates movement of substances.

questions.text: The cell wall of plant cells is made mainly of
questions.explanation: Cellulose gives the plant cell wall strength.

questions.text: Which organelle stores cell sap in plant cells?
questions.explanation: The vacuole holds cell sap and keeps the cell firm.

questions.text: Which of the following is found in both plant and animal cells?
questions.explanation: Both plant and animal cells respire, so both contain mitochondria.

questions.text: Which instrument is used to see the fine details of organelles such as ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are too small for a light microscope; an electron microscope is needed.

questions.text: The jelly-like substance in which organelles are found is the
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions of the cell take place in the cytoplasm.

questions.text: Genetic material is found mainly in the
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes made of DNA.

questions.text: Mature red blood cells in humans have no
questions.explanation: Lacking a nucleus leaves more space for haemoglobin to carry oxygen.

questions.text: Which organelle packages and transports proteins in the cell?
questions.explanation: The Golgi body modifies, packs and sends out proteins.

questions.text: The cell theory states that
options: cells are found only in animals
all cells have a cell wall
all living things are made of cells
questions.explanation: The cell theory says cells are the basic unit of life and come from existing cells.

questions.text: Which part of the nucleus makes ribosomes?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus produces ribosomal material.

questions.text: Lysosomes in a cell are important because they
questions.explanation: Lysosomes break down worn-out parts and engulfed materials.

questions.text: Which feature is found in bacterial cells but not in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Bacteria have a cell wall; animal cells do not.

questions.text: In plant cells, chloroplasts are most numerous in the
questions.explanation: Palisade cells near the upper leaf surface receive the most light.

questions.text: The total magnification of a microscope with ×10 eyepiece and ×40 objective is
questions.explanation: Multiply the two: 10 × 40 = 400.

questions.text: Which stain is commonly used to show the nucleus in onion cells?
questions.explanation: Iodine stains the nucleus and makes cells easier to see.

questions.text: A cell that lacks chloroplasts but has a cell wall and a large vacuole is most likely
questions.explanation: Root cells are plant cells but receive no light, so they have no chloroplasts.

questions.text: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food in aerobic respiration.

questions.text: The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of membranes that
questions.explanation: The ER forms channels for moving substances; rough ER carries ribosomes.

questions.text: Which cell is adapted for carrying messages around the body?
questions.explanation: Nerve cells (neurones) have long fibres to carry impulses.

questions.text: Guard cells are found
questions.explanation: Pairs of guard cells open and close the stomata.

questions.text: The cell wall is described as fully permeable because it
options: allows most substances to pass through
questions.explanation: Unlike the membrane, the cell wall does not control entry of substances.

questions.text: Which of these organisms has cells without a true nucleus?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes; their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm.

questions.text: Which feature allows a root hair cell to absorb water efficiently?
options: its lack of a cell membrane
its long, thin extension giving a large surface area
questions.explanation: The root hair extension greatly increases surface area for absorption.

questions.text: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of
options: low pressure to high pressure only
questions.explanation: Particles spread out down a concentration gradient.

questions.text: Osmosis needs a
questions.explanation: Osmosis is diffusion of water through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.text: A plant cell placed in pure water becomes

questions.text: The shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall in a concentrated solution is called
questions.explanation: Water leaves the vacuole by osmosis, pulling the membrane away from the wall.

questions.text: A red blood cell placed in a concentrated salt solution will
questions.explanation: Water leaves the cell by osmosis, so it shrinks (crenates).

questions.text: The bursting of red blood cells placed in water is called
questions.explanation: Water floods in by osmosis and, without a cell wall, the cell bursts.

questions.text: Which factor increases the rate of diffusion?
questions.explanation: Particles move faster at higher temperatures.

questions.text: Active transport differs from diffusion because it
options: uses energy to move substances against a concentration gradient
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy from respiration.

questions.text: Root hair cells take up mineral ions from soil with low concentrations by

questions.text: Fresh vegetables kept in salted water become limp because
options: salt enters and makes them swell
water leaves their cells by osmosis
questions.explanation: The salty solution is more concentrated than the cell sap.

questions.text: Oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood by
questions.explanation: Oxygen diffuses from high concentration in the air sacs to lower concentration in blood.

questions.text: Turgidity in plant cells helps to

questions.text: A solution with a higher water concentration than the cell contents is described as
questions.explanation: Water enters cells placed in a hypotonic solution.

questions.text: A solution with the same concentration as the cell contents is
questions.explanation: There is no net movement of water in an isotonic solution.

questions.text: Why do plants wilt on a hot, dry afternoon?
options: their cells lose turgor as water is lost faster than it is absorbed

options: bacteria lose water by osmosis and die
salt adds water to the fish
questions.explanation: The salt draws water out of microorganisms, preventing decay.

questions.text: Which is NOT a factor affecting the rate of diffusion?

questions.text: A potato strip placed in strong sugar solution becomes

questions.explanation: It diffuses from the air, where it is more concentrated, into the leaf.

questions.text: Which statement about osmosis is correct?
options: it involves water molecules moving through a membrane
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.text: Wilted vegetables become firm again when placed in clean water because
options: water enters their cells by osmosis
they carry out photosynthesis in water
questions.explanation: The cells take in water and regain turgor.

questions.text: The word equation for photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: Plants use light energy and chlorophyll to make glucose and release oxygen.

questions.text: In which part of the cell does photosynthesis take place?

questions.text: The pigment that traps light energy for photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

questions.text: Before testing a leaf for starch, it is boiled in alcohol to

questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black when starch is present.

questions.text: A plant is destarched by
options: keeping it in darkness for about two days
questions.explanation: In darkness the plant uses up its stored starch.

questions.text: Soda lime is used in photosynthesis experiments to

questions.text: The gas released during photosynthesis comes from
questions.explanation: Water molecules are split in the light stage, releasing oxygen.

questions.text: Which factor is NOT needed for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a product, not a requirement.

questions.text: The first product of photosynthesis that is easily detected in leaves is
questions.explanation: Glucose made is quickly converted to starch for storage.

questions.text: Magnesium deficiency in plants causes

questions.text: Plants such as mistletoe that live on another plant and take food from it are
questions.explanation: Mistletoe draws water and minerals from its host.

questions.text: Organisms that make their own food from simple substances are called
questions.explanation: Green plants are autotrophs.

questions.text: Which mineral element is important for root growth in plants?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus encourages strong roots.

questions.text: Nitrogen is needed by plants mainly to make
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is part of amino acids and proteins.

questions.text: Increasing light intensity increases the rate of photosynthesis up to a point because
options: another factor such as carbon dioxide then becomes limiting
questions.explanation: Beyond a point, rate is limited by another factor such as CO₂ or temperature.

questions.text: The light stage of photosynthesis produces
questions.explanation: Light splits water, releasing oxygen and making ATP and reduced carriers.

questions.text: The dark stage of photosynthesis is also called the
questions.explanation: It uses carbon dioxide to make sugars and does not need light directly.

questions.text: Variegated leaves are useful in experiments to show that photosynthesis needs

questions.text: Which of the following organisms is a saprophyte?
questions.explanation: Saprophytes feed on dead and decaying matter.

questions.text: The broad, flat shape of a leaf helps photosynthesis because it
options: gives a large surface area to absorb light
questions.explanation: More surface means more light and carbon dioxide can be absorbed.

questions.text: The air spaces in the spongy mesophyll help photosynthesis by
options: allowing gases to diffuse to the cells
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide spreads through the air spaces to the photosynthesising cells.

questions.text: When a green plant is in bright light, which gas is it releasing in the greatest amount?
questions.explanation: In bright light photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so there is net oxygen release.

questions.text: Bubbles given off by a water plant such as Elodea in light are mainly

questions.text: All the populations living and interacting in an area form a

questions.text: The place where an organism lives is its

questions.text: A community together with its non-living environment is an
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes living things and their physical surroundings.

questions.text: Organisms that feed only on plants are
questions.explanation: Herbivores such as goats are primary consumers.

questions.text: Which organism is an omnivore?
questions.explanation: Humans eat both plant and animal food.

questions.text: In a food chain, energy is lost at each level mainly as
questions.explanation: Organisms use energy and lose much of it as heat, so less passes on.

questions.text: A food web is
options: the number of animals in a habitat
questions.explanation: Most animals eat more than one food, so food chains link into webs.

questions.text: Which organism occupies the first trophic level?
questions.explanation: Producers (green plants) start every food chain.

questions.text: In a pyramid of energy, the base represents
questions.explanation: Producers hold the most energy, so they form the wide base.

questions.text: Why are food chains rarely longer than five links?
options: too little energy is left at the higher levels
animals cannot eat more than one food
questions.explanation: About 90% of energy is lost at each level.

questions.text: The relationship in which one organism benefits and the other is neither harmed nor helped is
questions.explanation: In commensalism only one partner benefits.

questions.text: Lichen is an example of
options: mutualism between an alga and a fungus
questions.explanation: The alga makes food and the fungus provides water and shelter.

questions.text: A hawk feeding on chicks is an example of
questions.explanation: The predator kills and eats its prey.

questions.text: Competition between organisms is most likely when they
questions.explanation: Competition happens when resources such as food or space are scarce.

questions.text: The role an organism plays in its ecosystem is its

questions.text: Which group of organisms returns nutrients from dead bodies to the soil?
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead matter.

questions.text: In the food chain maize → rat → snake → eagle, the snake is a
questions.explanation: The snake eats a primary consumer (the rat).

questions.explanation: Energy decreases along the chain, so the top carnivore has least.

questions.text: A pyramid of numbers can be inverted when
options: one large tree supports many insects
questions.explanation: A single big producer can feed many small herbivores, inverting the pyramid.

questions.text: Tick feeding on a cow is an example of
questions.explanation: The tick benefits and the cow is harmed.

questions.text: The total mass of living organisms at each trophic level is shown in a pyramid of
questions.explanation: A biomass pyramid shows the dry mass at each level.

questions.text: Which of these is an aquatic producer?
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton are tiny plants that photosynthesise in water.

questions.text: Removing all snakes from a farm would most likely lead to
options: an increase in the rat population
questions.explanation: Snakes eat rats, so without them rats multiply.

questions.text: Organisms that feed on dead organic matter such as millipedes are

questions.text: The earthworm is supported by
questions.explanation: Fluid under pressure in its body supports the earthworm.

questions.text: Red blood cells are made in the
questions.explanation: Red bone marrow produces blood cells.

questions.text: Which tissue joins one bone to another at a joint?

questions.text: The knee is an example of a
questions.explanation: The knee moves mainly in one plane, like a door hinge.

questions.text: The joint between the skull bones is an example of a
questions.explanation: The skull bones are joined by sutures that do not move.

questions.text: The joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae, which lets the head turn, is a
questions.explanation: The atlas rotates round a peg on the axis.

questions.text: Synovial fluid in a joint
questions.explanation: It reduces friction so bones move smoothly.

questions.text: Cartilage at the ends of bones
questions.explanation: Smooth cartilage cushions the bones at joints.

questions.text: Muscles that work in pairs, one contracting while the other relaxes, are called
questions.explanation: The biceps and triceps are a classic antagonistic pair.

questions.text: Contraction of the biceps causes the arm to
questions.explanation: The biceps pulls the forearm up, bending the elbow.

questions.text: Which vertebrae are found in the neck?

questions.text: The ribs are attached to the
questions.explanation: Thoracic vertebrae carry facets for the ribs.

questions.text: The largest and strongest vertebrae, found in the lower back, are the
questions.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae carry much of the body's weight.

questions.text: The bone of the upper arm is the
questions.explanation: The humerus runs from shoulder to elbow.

questions.text: The longest bone in the human body is the

questions.text: Which of the following is a ball and socket joint?

questions.text: Lack of vitamin D in children may cause
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium for strong bones.

questions.text: In plants, support is provided mainly by

questions.text: The exoskeleton of insects is made mainly of
questions.explanation: Chitin forms a tough outer covering.

questions.text: A disadvantage of an exoskeleton is that
options: the animal must moult to grow
questions.explanation: The hard covering cannot grow, so it is shed and replaced.

questions.text: The shoulder blade is the
questions.explanation: The scapula is a flat, triangular bone at the back of the shoulder.

questions.text: Which part of the skeleton protects the spinal cord?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord runs through the neural canal of the vertebrae.

questions.explanation: Benedict's solution changes from blue to brick red with reducing sugars such as glucose.

questions.text: The colour of Benedict's solution before any test is
questions.explanation: Benedict's solution is blue because it contains copper(II) sulphate.

questions.text: A sample gives a translucent spot on paper that does not dry out. The sample contains

questions.text: Sudan III solution is used to test for
questions.explanation: Sudan III stains fats red.

questions.text: Which food would give a positive result with Millon's reagent?

questions.text: Enzymes are described as biological catalysts because they

questions.text: The substance an enzyme acts on is called its

questions.text: Most human enzymes work best at about
questions.explanation: Human enzymes are adapted to body temperature.

questions.text: Enzymes are specific. This means each enzyme

questions.text: Proteins are digested into

options: work slowly but are not destroyed
questions.explanation: Cold slows molecules and reactions; the enzyme recovers when warmed.

questions.text: An enzyme that has lost its shape due to heat is said to be

questions.text: The capital market deals in
questions.explanation: The capital market provides long-term finance, for example through shares and bonds.

questions.text: Which tool does the Central Bank use to reduce money supply?
questions.explanation: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive, reducing money in circulation.

questions.text: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total value of
options: goods and services produced within a country in a year
questions.explanation: GDP measures output within the country's borders.

questions.text: GNP is equal to GDP plus
questions.explanation: GNP adds income earned by citizens abroad and subtracts income paid to foreigners.

questions.text: Per capita income is
questions.explanation: It shows average income per person.

questions.text: Which method of measuring national income adds up all incomes earned?
questions.explanation: The income approach sums wages, rent, interest and profit.

questions.text: Net National Product is GNP minus
questions.explanation: Depreciation (capital consumption) is the wear and tear of capital goods.

questions.text: Which problem can make national income figures inaccurate?
options: many activities are not recorded, such as subsistence farming
questions.explanation: Unrecorded informal and subsistence output leads to underestimation.

questions.text: A tax whose rate rises as income rises is a
questions.explanation: Personal income tax in many countries is progressive.

questions.text: Which of these is an indirect tax?
questions.explanation: Indirect taxes are paid on goods and services, not directly on income.

questions.text: When government expenditure is greater than revenue, the budget is in
questions.explanation: A deficit budget spends more than it earns and is often financed by borrowing.

questions.text: The incidence of a tax refers to
options: who finally bears the burden of the tax
questions.explanation: A tax on a seller may be passed on to buyers through higher prices.

questions.text: Which is a canon (principle) of taxation?
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's canons include certainty, convenience, economy and equality.

questions.text: Money borrowed by the government from its own citizens is called
questions.explanation: Domestic debt is raised within the country, for example through treasury bills and bonds.

questions.text: The theory of comparative cost advantage was developed by
questions.explanation: Ricardo showed that countries gain by specialising where their opportunity cost is lowest.

questions.text: The balance of trade is the difference between
options: the value of visible exports and visible imports
questions.explanation: Balance of trade covers only goods (visible items).

questions.text: A tax placed on imported goods is called a
questions.explanation: Tariffs make imports more expensive to protect local industries.

questions.text: A complete ban on trade with a country is called
questions.explanation: An embargo prohibits trade entirely.

questions.text: Devaluation of the naira makes Nigerian exports
questions.explanation: Foreigners get more naira for their currency, so Nigerian goods cost them less.

questions.text: Terms of trade measure
options: the ratio of export prices to import prices
questions.explanation: Terms of trade = (index of export prices ÷ index of import prices) × 100.

questions.text: ECOWAS was established in
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States was formed by the Treaty of Lagos in 1975.

questions.text: Nigeria is a member of OPEC because it is a major
questions.explanation: OPEC is the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.

questions.text: Which is a common feature of developing economies?
questions.explanation: Many developing economies rely on agriculture and raw material exports.

questions.text: Economic development differs from economic growth because development includes
options: improvements in living standards and welfare
questions.explanation: Growth is a rise in output; development also considers health, education and welfare.

questions.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) mainly helps countries with
questions.explanation: The IMF provides short-term support to stabilise countries' external payments.

questions.text: Which sector currently earns Nigeria most of its foreign exchange?
questions.explanation: Petroleum exports have dominated Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings since the 1970s.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "frugal" in this sentence: My uncle lives a frugal life.
questions.explanation: A frugal person is careful not to waste money.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "candid" in this sentence: Thank you for your candid advice.
questions.explanation: Candid advice is honest and direct.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "hostile" in this sentence: The crowd was hostile to the visitors.
questions.explanation: "Hostile" means showing opposition or dislike.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "eminent" in this sentence: An eminent surgeon visited our school.
questions.explanation: An eminent person is famous and respected.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "meagre" in this sentence: He survives on a meagre salary.
questions.explanation: "Meagre" means too small in amount.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "imminent" in this sentence: The storm is imminent.
questions.explanation: "Imminent" means likely to happen very soon. Do not confuse it with "eminent".

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "rectify" in this sentence: Please rectify the error in your work.
questions.explanation: To rectify is to put right.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to "ponder" in this sentence: She pondered the question for a while.
questions.explanation: To ponder is to think about something carefully.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "optimistic" in this sentence: Bisi is optimistic about the result.
questions.explanation: An optimist expects good outcomes; a pessimist expects bad ones.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "expand" in this sentence: The company plans to expand.
questions.explanation: To expand is to grow larger; to contract is to become smaller.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "visible" in this sentence: The mountain was visible from the road.
questions.explanation: "Visible" means able to be seen.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "courageous" in this sentence: The courageous soldier saved his friend.
questions.explanation: A courageous person is brave; a cowardly person lacks courage.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "inferior" in this sentence: This cloth is of inferior quality.
questions.explanation: "Inferior" means lower in quality; "superior" means higher.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "accept" in this sentence: She accepted the gift.
questions.explanation: To reject is to refuse to accept.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "punctual" in this sentence: Femi is always punctual.
questions.explanation: A punctual person arrives on time.

questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to "ascend" in this sentence: The climbers ascended the hill.
questions.explanation: To ascend is to go up; to descend is to go down.

questions.text: What does "to bury the hatchet" mean?
options: to make peace after a quarrel
questions.explanation: The idiom means to end a disagreement.

questions.text: What does "to turn over a new leaf" mean?
options: to change one's behaviour for the better
questions.explanation: It means to start behaving better.

questions.text: What does "to beat about the bush" mean?
questions.explanation: Someone who beats about the bush does not get to the point.

questions.text: What does "a wet blanket" refer to?
options: a blanket left in the rain
a person who spoils other people's fun
questions.explanation: A wet blanket discourages others from enjoying themselves.

questions.text: What does "at the eleventh hour" mean?
options: in the middle of the day
questions.explanation: Something done at the eleventh hour is done just in time.

questions.text: What does "to have cold feet" mean?
options: to become nervous and want to back out
questions.explanation: Someone with cold feet loses courage before an important event.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Between you and ___, the plan will fail.
questions.explanation: After a preposition ("between"), use the object pronoun "me".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Everyone should bring ___ own textbook.
questions.explanation: "Their" shows possession; it is commonly used after "everyone".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: It was ___ who broke the window.
questions.explanation: After "it was", formal English uses the subject pronoun "he".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The two friends helped each ___.
questions.explanation: "Each other" is used for two people; "one another" is often used for more than two.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: I have ___ money left, so I can't buy lunch.
questions.explanation: "Little" (without "a") means almost none; "few" is used with countable nouns.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.explanation: Use "an" before a vowel sound; the "h" in "honest" is silent.

questions.text: What is the plural of "child"?
questions.explanation: "Child" has an irregular plural, "children".

questions.text: What is the plural of "criterion"?
questions.explanation: "Criterion" comes from Greek, and its plural is "criteria".

questions.text: What is the plural of "mother-in-law"?
questions.explanation: The main word, "mother", takes the plural ending.

questions.text: Which of these nouns has no plural form in standard English?
questions.explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable: say "pieces of furniture".

questions.text: What is the plural of "analysis"?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in "-is" often change to "-es": crisis → crises, thesis → theses.

questions.text: What is the plural of "phenomenon"?
questions.explanation: Like "criterion", "phenomenon" changes "-on" to "-a".

questions.text: In which word is the "b" silent?
questions.explanation: The "b" in "doubt", "debt", "lamb" and "thumb" is not pronounced.

questions.text: In which word is the "t" silent?
questions.explanation: "Listen", "castle" and "whistle" have a silent "t".

questions.text: In which word is the "w" silent?
questions.explanation: The "w" in "write", "wrist" and "wrong" is silent.

questions.text: In which word is the "h" silent?
questions.explanation: "Hour", "honest" and "heir" begin with a vowel sound.

questions.text: In which word is the "g" silent?
questions.explanation: In "sign" the "g" is silent, but in "signal" it is pronounced.

questions.text: In which word is the "l" silent?
questions.explanation: The "l" in "calm", "walk", "talk" and "half" is silent.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "bread"?
questions.explanation: "Bread" and "said" both end in /ed/, despite the different spellings.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "gone"?
questions.explanation: "Gone" and "on" share the vowel /ɒ/ in British English.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "wear"?
questions.explanation: "Wear" and "chair" end with the same sound /eə/.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "laugh"?
questions.explanation: "Laugh" and "half" both end in /ɑːf/.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "key"?
questions.explanation: Both end in the long vowel /iː/.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with "love"?
questions.explanation: "Love" and "dove" share /ʌv/. "Move" has /uː/ and "stove" has /əʊ/.

questions.text: In the sentence "AMAKA bought the red dress", the capital letters show the stressed word. Which question does it answer?
options: Did Amaka sell the red dress?
questions.explanation: Stressing "Amaka" shows that the important information is who did it.

questions.text: In "Amaka bought the RED dress", which question is answered?
options: Did Amaka buy the red shoes?
Did Amaka borrow the red dress?
questions.explanation: The stress on "red" contrasts it with dresses of other colours.

questions.text: In "Amaka BOUGHT the red dress", which question is answered?
options: What colour was the dress Amaka bought?
Did Amaka borrow the red dress?
Did Amaka buy the red shoes?
questions.explanation: Stressing the verb contrasts buying with another action, such as borrowing.

questions.text: In "The bus left at SEVEN o'clock", which question is answered?
options: Did the car leave at seven o'clock?
Did the bus leave at six o'clock?
Did the bus arrive at seven o'clock?
questions.explanation: The stress on "seven" corrects a wrong time.

questions.text: In "My father drives a TAXI", which question is answered?
options: Does your father ride a taxi?
Does your father drive a bus?
Does your mother drive a taxi?
questions.explanation: Stressing "taxi" contrasts it with another vehicle.

questions.text: In "We are travelling to Kano TOMORROW", which question is answered?
options: Are you travelling to Kano today?
Are you travelling to Kaduna tomorrow?
Who is travelling to Kano tomorrow?
Are you flying to Kano tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Stressing "tomorrow" shows the important information is the time.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ indoors.
questions.explanation: A real (first) conditional uses "if + present" with "will".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I had known, I ___ you.
questions.explanation: An impossible past (third) conditional uses "had + past participle" and "would have".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If water ___ to 100 °C, it boils.
questions.explanation: General truths (zero conditional) use the present in both clauses.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not": if you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Had she studied harder, she ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: "Had she studied" is an inverted form of "If she had studied".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I ___ a bird, I would fly home.
questions.explanation: In unreal present conditions, formal English uses "were" for all persons.

questions.text: Which prefix gives "possible" its opposite meaning?
questions.explanation: "Impossible". Before p, b and m, "in-" usually becomes "im-".

questions.text: Which prefix gives "agree" its opposite meaning?
questions.explanation: "Disagree".

questions.text: Which word is formed by adding a suffix to make a noun from "happy"?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-ness" forms a noun; "-ly" forms an adverb.

questions.text: What is the adjective form of "danger"?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-ous" forms an adjective.

questions.text: What is the verb form of "strength"?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-en" forms verbs such as "strengthen", "widen" and "shorten".

questions.text: The prefix "pre-" in "prepaid" means
questions.explanation: Prepaid means paid in advance.

questions.text: "Please close the door." What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences give orders, requests or instructions.

questions.text: "What a beautiful day!" What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences express strong feeling and end with an exclamation mark.

questions.text: A sentence with one main clause and at least one subordinate clause is a
questions.explanation: For example: "I stayed at home because I was ill."

questions.text: "I wanted to go, but it was raining." What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Two main clauses are joined by the coordinating conjunction "but".

questions.text: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: When the dog barked, we woke up.
The dog barked and the cat ran.
The dog barked because it saw a stranger.
questions.explanation: A simple sentence has only one clause.

questions.text: "Is the library open today?" What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: Interrogative sentences ask questions.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By next year, I ___ in this school for five years.
questions.explanation: The future perfect shows a duration completed by a future time.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She ___ her homework before her mother came home.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Water ___ at 100 °C at sea level.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts use the simple present.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Mathematics ___ my best subject.
questions.explanation: Subjects ending in "-ics" such as Mathematics and Physics take a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: "A number of" means "many" and takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The committee ___ divided in their opinions.
questions.explanation: When the members act as individuals ("their opinions"), the collective noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He has been ill ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: "Since" is used with a point in time; "for" is used with a period of time.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The thief broke ___ the house at night.
questions.explanation: To "break into" a building means to enter it by force.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is married ___ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The correct expression is "married to".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students were asked to hand ___ their assignments.
questions.explanation: To "hand in" means to submit.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The prize was shared between Tunde and ___.
questions.explanation: After a preposition such as "between", use the object pronoun "me".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: ___ of the two answers is correct.
questions.explanation: "Neither" refers to two things; "none" is used for more than two.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: This book is ___; you can borrow it.
questions.explanation: "Mine" is a possessive pronoun that stands alone.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students ___ cleaned the classroom.
questions.explanation: The emphatic pronoun for "students" is "themselves".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Is this the man ___ car was stolen?
questions.explanation: "Whose" shows possession.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The girl ___ you met yesterday is my cousin.
questions.explanation: "Whom" is the object of "met".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: ___ students in our class passed the test.
questions.explanation: "All the" goes with a plural noun.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: We bought ___ oranges at the market.
questions.explanation: Use "some" in positive statements with plural countable nouns.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Have you got ___ questions?
questions.explanation: "Any" is normally used in questions.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: There isn't ___ sugar left in the tin.
questions.explanation: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns such as sugar.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Only ___ people came to the meeting, so it was cancelled.
questions.explanation: "A few" goes with countable plural nouns.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: ___ of my brothers is in the army.
questions.explanation: "One of my brothers is" takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She bought ___ umbrella yesterday.
questions.explanation: Use "an" before a vowel sound.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Kofi is ___ university student.
questions.explanation: "University" begins with a "yoo" sound, so it takes "a".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He gave ___ an hour to finish the work.
questions.explanation: "Us" is the object pronoun.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: It is ___ responsibility to keep the school clean.
questions.explanation: The possessive of "everybody" is "everybody's".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The dog wagged ___ tail.
questions.explanation: "Its" is the possessive form; "it's" means "it is".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: You and ___ should represent the class.
questions.explanation: It is part of the subject, so use "I".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: ___ of the students has a calculator.
questions.explanation: "Each" takes a singular verb: "Each ... has".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The books on the shelf are ___.
questions.explanation: "Theirs" is the possessive pronoun that stands alone.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: This is the house ___ Jack built.
questions.explanation: "That" (or "which") refers to things.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: I have ___ little money, but it is enough.
questions.explanation: "A little" means some, though not much.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: ___ is knocking at the door?
questions.explanation: "Who" is the subject of "is knocking".

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Both of ___ are going to the party.
questions.explanation: After "of", use the object pronoun "them".

questions.text: What is the plural of "ox"?
questions.explanation: "Oxen" is an irregular plural.

questions.text: What is the plural of "tooth"?
questions.explanation: The vowel changes: tooth → teeth.

questions.text: What is the plural of "mouse" (the animal)?
questions.explanation: Mouse → mice.

questions.text: What is the plural of "crisis"?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -is change to -es.

questions.text: What is the plural of "datum"?
questions.explanation: "Data" comes from Latin.

questions.text: What is the plural of "medium" (a means of communication)?
questions.explanation: "The media" is the plural of "medium" in this sense.

questions.text: What is the plural of "passer-by"?
questions.explanation: The main word "passer" takes the plural.

questions.text: What is the plural of "knife"?
questions.explanation: Many nouns ending in -fe change to -ves.

questions.text: What is the plural of "roof"?
questions.explanation: "Roof" simply adds -s.

questions.text: What is the plural of "potato"?
questions.explanation: Some nouns ending in -o add -es.

questions.text: What is the plural of "piano"?
questions.explanation: "Piano" just adds -s.

questions.text: What is the plural of "sheep"?
questions.explanation: "Sheep" has the same form in singular and plural.

questions.text: What is the plural of "lady"?
questions.explanation: A consonant + y changes to -ies.

questions.text: What is the plural of "monkey"?
questions.explanation: A vowel + y simply adds -s.

questions.text: What is the plural of "bus"?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -s add -es.

questions.text: What is the plural of "woman"?
questions.explanation: Woman → women.

questions.text: What is the plural of "louse"?
questions.explanation: Louse → lice, like mouse → mice.

questions.text: What is the plural of "basis"?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -is change to -es.

questions.text: What is the plural of "fungus"?
questions.explanation: The Latin plural "fungi" is standard in science.

questions.text: Which of these nouns is always plural?
questions.explanation: "Scissors" is used only in plural form.

questions.text: Which of these is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: "Luggage" has no plural; we say "pieces of luggage".

questions.text: What is the plural of "commander-in-chief"?
questions.explanation: The main noun "commander" takes the plural.

questions.text: What is the plural of "half"?
questions.explanation: Half → halves.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
options: A furnitures is in the room.
The furnitures in the room are new.
The furnitures in the room is new.
The furniture in the room is new.
questions.explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: In which word is the "k" silent?
questions.explanation: The "k" before "n" at the start of a word is silent.

questions.text: In which word is the "p" silent?
questions.explanation: Initial "ps" is pronounced "s".

questions.text: In which word is the "n" silent?
questions.explanation: Final "mn" sounds like "m".

questions.text: In which word is the "c" silent?
questions.explanation: "Muscle" sounds like "mussel".

questions.text: In which word is the "d" silent?
questions.explanation: "Wednesday" is pronounced "Wenzday".

questions.text: In which word is the "s" silent?
questions.explanation: "Island" is pronounced "eye-land".

questions.text: In which word is the "u" silent?
questions.explanation: In "guest" the "u" only hardens the "g".

questions.text: In which word is the "h" silent?
questions.explanation: "Honest" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.text: In which word is the "gh" silent?
questions.explanation: In "night", "gh" makes no sound.

questions.text: In which word is the "b" silent?
questions.explanation: "Debt" is pronounced "det".

questions.text: In which word is the "t" silent?
questions.explanation: The "t" in "whistle" is not pronounced.

questions.text: In which word is the "w" silent?
questions.explanation: "Answer" is pronounced "an-ser".

questions.text: In which word is the "l" silent?
questions.explanation: "Walk" is pronounced "wawk".

questions.text: In which word is the "g" silent?
questions.explanation: "Foreign" ends in an "n" sound.

questions.text: Which word has a silent "e" at the end?
questions.explanation: The final "e" in "hope" is not sounded but lengthens the "o".

questions.text: In which word is the "ch" pronounced as /k/?
questions.explanation: Words from Greek such as "chorus" use /k/.

questions.text: In which word is "ch" pronounced as /ʃ/ (as in "she")?
questions.explanation: "Machine" comes from French and uses /ʃ/.

questions.text: In which word is the "th" pronounced as /ð/ (as in "this")?
questions.explanation: "Brother" has the voiced /ð/ sound.

questions.text: In which word is "ph" pronounced as /f/?
questions.explanation: "Ph" in "photograph" sounds like "f".

questions.text: Which word has a silent letter?
questions.explanation: The "t" in "castle" is silent.

questions.text: In which word is the "r" not pronounced in standard British English?
questions.explanation: In British English, "r" at the end of a word before a pause is not sounded.

questions.text: In which word is the "c" pronounced as /s/?
questions.explanation: "C" before i, e or y usually sounds like /s/.

questions.text: In which word is the "g" pronounced as /dʒ/ (as in "jam")?
questions.explanation: "G" before i can sound like /dʒ/, as in "giant".

questions.text: In which word is the "s" pronounced as /z/?
questions.explanation: "Easy" has a /z/ sound in the middle.

questions.text: "Lagos is a busy city." What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: It states a fact.

questions.text: "Sit down quietly." What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: It gives a command.

questions.text: "How fast she runs!" What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: It expresses strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.text: "Where did you keep the keys?" What type of sentence is this?
questions.explanation: It asks a question.

questions.text: A sentence with two or more main clauses joined by a conjunction is a
questions.explanation: E.g. "I called, and she answered."

questions.text: "When the bell rang, the students went home." This is a
questions.explanation: It has a main clause and a subordinate clause beginning with "when".

questions.text: Which of these is a compound sentence?
options: She was tired, so she went to bed.
Although she was tired, she worked.
questions.explanation: Two main clauses are joined by "so".

questions.text: Which of these is a sentence fragment?
options: We waited because the road was flooded.
The road was flooded, so we waited.
questions.explanation: It has no main clause, so it is incomplete.

questions.text: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: My brother plays football every Saturday.
My brother, who is tall, plays football.
If it rains, my brother stays home.
My brother plays football, and I watch.
questions.explanation: It has only one clause.

questions.text: The subject of the sentence "The old farmer sold his goats" is
questions.explanation: The subject is who does the action.

questions.text: In "The teacher marked the scripts", the object is
questions.explanation: The object receives the action.

questions.text: "Please pass me the salt." This sentence makes
questions.explanation: It is a polite imperative.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a complement?
questions.explanation: "A nurse" completes the meaning of "is".

questions.text: A sentence which has a main clause and two subordinate clauses is a
questions.explanation: Any sentence with at least one subordinate clause is complex.

questions.text: "What time does the train leave?" begins with
questions.explanation: "What" is a wh-question word.

questions.text: Which is a compound-complex sentence?
options: When the rain stopped, we left, and they stayed.

questions.text: The disjunction p ∨ q is false when

both p and q are true
questions.explanation: "Or" is true if at least one part is true.

questions.explanation: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (100 × 4) ÷ 200 = 2 L.

questions.text: Charles's law relates the volume of a gas to its
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to temperature in kelvin.

questions.text: A gas has a volume of 300 cm³ at 300 K. What is its volume at 600 K if pressure is constant?
questions.explanation: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂, so V₂ = 300 × 600 ÷ 300 = 600 cm³.

questions.text: What is absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero is 0 K, which is about −273 °C.

questions.text: According to the kinetic theory, gas pressure is caused by
options: heat flowing out of the gas
gas molecules colliding with the walls of the container
questions.explanation: Moving molecules hit the walls and change momentum, producing a force on the walls.

questions.text: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 4 m. What is its speed?
Which of these is a longitudinal wave?
questions.explanation: In sound waves the particles vibrate along the direction the wave travels.

questions.text: Which of these waves can travel through a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light is an electromagnetic wave and needs no material medium.

questions.text: The maximum displacement of a wave from its rest position is called its
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the height of a crest (or depth of a trough) from the rest position.

questions.text: A wave has a period of 0.02 s. What is its frequency?
Which electromagnetic wave is used for TV remote controls?
questions.explanation: Most TV remote controls send coded pulses of infrared radiation.

questions.text: Sound travels fastest through
questions.explanation: Particles are closest together in solids, so vibrations pass on fastest. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.text: A boy hears the echo of his shout from a cliff 2 s after shouting. If sound travels at 340 m/s, how far is the cliff?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back: 2d = 340 × 2, so d = 340 m.

questions.text: The pitch of a sound depends on its
questions.explanation: Higher frequency gives a higher pitch.

questions.text: The loudness of a sound depends on its
questions.explanation: The bigger the amplitude of vibration, the louder the sound.

questions.text: Why can't sound travel through space?
options: there is no medium for the sound to travel through
questions.explanation: Sound needs particles (a medium) to pass on its vibrations.

questions.text: What property of sound allows us to tell a guitar from a piano playing the same note?
questions.explanation: Quality depends on the overtones each instrument produces.

questions.text: The angle of incidence on a plane mirror is 30°. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: By the laws of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

questions.text: Which of these describes an image in a plane mirror?
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image the same size as the object, but left and right are swapped.

questions.text: A pool of water looks shallower than it really is because of
questions.explanation: Light bends away from the normal as it leaves the water, making the bottom appear raised.

questions.text: Light travels from air into glass with a refractive index of 1.5. If the speed of light in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, what is its speed in glass?
questions.explanation: n = speed in air ÷ speed in glass, so speed in glass = 3 × 10⁸ ÷ 1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.text: The splitting of white light into its colours by a prism is called
questions.explanation: Each colour is refracted by a different amount, so white light spreads into a spectrum.

questions.text: Which mirror is used as a driving mirror because it gives a wide field of view?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an upright, diminished image covering a wide area.

questions.text: A current of 2 A flows through a resistor of 6 Ω. What is the voltage across it?
What is the total resistance of 3 Ω and 6 Ω resistors connected in series?
questions.explanation: In series, R = R₁ + R₂ = 3 + 6 = 9 Ω.

questions.text: What is the total resistance of 3 Ω and 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel?
An electric iron is rated 1000 W. How much energy does it use in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 1 kW × 2 h = 2 kWh.

questions.text: Which instrument is connected in series to measure current?
questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series so that all the current passes through it.

questions.text: What is the function of a fuse in a circuit?
options: to break the circuit when too much current flows
questions.explanation: The thin fuse wire melts when the current is too high, protecting the appliance.

questions.text: Like magnetic poles
options: have no effect on each other
questions.explanation: Two north poles or two south poles push each other away.

questions.text: Which material is best for making a permanent magnet?
questions.explanation: Steel is hard to magnetise but keeps its magnetism. Soft iron loses it easily.

questions.text: Which device changes mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: A generator turns a coil in a magnetic field to produce electricity.

questions.text: A transformer has 100 turns in the primary coil and 500 turns in the secondary. If the input is 20 V, what is the output?
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, so Vs = 20 × 500 ÷ 100 = 100 V. It is a step-up transformer.

questions.text: Why does a transformer work only with alternating current?
options: it needs a changing magnetic field to induce a voltage
direct current flows in both directions
alternating current has no magnetic field
questions.explanation: Induction needs a changing magnetic field, which only alternating current provides.

questions.text: Which device uses an electromagnet to make a hammer strike a gong?
questions.explanation: In an electric bell, an electromagnet pulls the hammer repeatedly to strike the gong.

questions.text: Which radiation is the most penetrating?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays can pass through several centimetres of lead. Alpha particles are stopped by paper.

questions.text: An alpha particle is the same as
questions.explanation: An alpha particle has 2 protons and 2 neutrons, like a helium nucleus.

questions.text: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 2 days. What fraction remains after 6 days?
questions.explanation: 6 days is 3 half-lives: ½ × ½ × ½ = 1/8.

questions.text: The splitting of a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei, releasing energy, is called
questions.explanation: Fission splits heavy nuclei such as uranium-235. Fusion joins light nuclei together.

questions.text: What particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons. Electrons move around the nucleus.

questions.text: Which particle is emitted when a neutron in a nucleus changes into a proton?
questions.explanation: In beta decay a neutron becomes a proton and a fast electron (beta particle) is emitted.

questions.text: Which material is a semiconductor?
questions.explanation: Silicon and germanium are semiconductors: their conductivity lies between conductors and insulators.

questions.text: Which device allows current to flow in only one direction?
questions.explanation: A diode conducts when forward-biased and blocks current when reverse-biased.

questions.text: Changing alternating current into direct current is called
questions.explanation: A rectifier, made with diodes, converts AC to DC.

questions.text: Adding small amounts of impurities to a semiconductor to improve its conductivity is called
questions.explanation: Doping produces n-type or p-type semiconductors.

questions.text: Which device is commonly used to amplify signals?
questions.explanation: A transistor can amplify small signals and act as a switch.

questions.text: A capacitor is a device that
options: converts AC to DC on its own
questions.explanation: A capacitor stores charge on two plates separated by an insulator.
